history.period: Main murti believed 100+ years old (per hindu-blog.com, unverified)
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: many shrines named 'Hari Mandir' exist across Dhanbad district; this file documents the well-known Hirapur temple at Pandey Muhalla, Harimandir Road, Dhanbad-826001 (0.7 km from Dhanbad Junction). Dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Hari), its main murti is an ashtadhatu (eight-metal) Radha Krishna believed to be more than 100 years old. The sanctum also houses a Shivling and an idol of Mahaprabhu (Gaurnitai); the one-acre complex additionally has murtis of Hanuman, Kali and Durga. The main temple's architecture is described as mehraab (arched) style. No authoritative founding record found; founding date UNVERIFIED. Main festivals are Sri Krishna Jayanti and Shivratri, with a special puja on Magh Purnima.

name: Hari Mandir, Dhanbad
town_description: Dhanbad is the second-largest city in Jharkhand and is widely known as the Coal Capital of India, home to extensive coal mines and the headquarters of Bharat Coking Coal Limited. It is a major railway junction on the Grand Chord line and hosts the Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), established in 1926. The city mixes an industrial character with green belts and serves as a gateway to nearby attractions like the Maithon and Panchet dams, Topchanchi Lake and the Parasnath Hills.
